status: experimental interoperability architecture; no legal-compliance claim
purpose: Define how data, claims, proofs, and metadata may cross institutional or jurisdictional boundaries while preserving local residency, minimization, selective disclosure, and explicit authority semantics.
core_invariants: data residency and disclosure scope are separate dimensions
a valid proof does not imply permission to disclose the underlying record
recipient recognition does not expand sender-side disclosure authority
cross-domain transfer requires exact purpose, audience, data class, residency, retention, and disclosure checks
privacy constraints compose conservatively by intersection
derived metadata is classified independently because metadata can itself be sensitive
offline or air-gapped transfer retains the same residency and disclosure obligations
local policy may narrow an imported recognition or disclosure profile
encrypted export does not by itself make an otherwise prohibited transfer permissible
proof-only and predicate-only modes should be preferred when they satisfy the relying party's legitimate verification need
nonclaims: This profile does not determine legal data residency obligations in any jurisdiction.
Encryption, tokenization, or pseudonymization does not automatically remove legal or ethical sensitivity.
Selective disclosure does not imply zero metadata leakage.
This profile does not create a universal privacy policy.
